claims.finding: The market had already fully reacted to this print before the filing that defines it: the results release and earnings call landed pre-open on 2026-09-01, the stock fell from a 2.89 prior close to 2.34 by 11:06 ET on 43.8m shares against a 19.8m twenty-day average, and closed at 2.39 — near the low — while the 6-K carrying the actual financial statements was not accepted until 20:52 UTC (16:52 ET), which puts the detailed disclosure inside the measured window rather than before it.

claims.why_not_priced: This is not a claim about the company being mispriced but about the event window being mis-specified, and nothing in the wire copy or in the baseline reflects it: the baseline books the 19.26% fall as run_up_5d_pct, i.e. it treats the reaction as run-in, and gives the name a null expected_move_pct with a 6.62% one-day-vol deadband, which would size a fresh earnings gap that cannot happen twice. What the window does contain is the after-the-close 6-K with the full statements on a day the stock closed on its low, which is where the detail gets read.
claims.independence: This shares its Stocktwits body with the finding below, which I flag rather than hide; the independent legs are seal.json's accepted_utc and quote.json's volume and price bars, both machine-generated and both from a different file in the capture than the thread.

claims.finding: On the 2026-09-01 call, disclosure quoted repeatedly in the pre-seal thread puts total cash at $100.5m but unrestricted cash at only $33.2m, against a roughly $300m buyback the company had announced, and management ended the call saying no online questions had been submitted — leaving the buyback and the 2027 outlook unaddressed — while H1 net loss was about $139m of which $67.5m was non-cash ($41.5m share-based comp, $20.4m D&A, $5.6m impairment).
claims.source: no URL in corpus; kind: social, stocktwits $RZLV thread fetched 2026-09-01T15:06:04Z
claims.why_not_priced: The intraday move priced the headline loss and the revenue reiteration; the unrestricted-versus-total cash split is a balance-sheet detail that only appears in the statements filed after the close, and the corpus contains zero news items for this name, so no sell-side or wire summary existed to propagate it. An issuer with $33.2m unrestricted cash that has filed two F-3 shelves (2025-11-28, 2025-12-19) and three prospectus supplements (424B7 2025-11-07, 424B3 2025-12-30, 424B5 2026-01-21) in the last ten months has an obvious next move, and a buyback nine times its unrestricted cash is not it.
claims.independence: Corroborated from a different file in the corpus rather than a different publisher: filings.json shows the serial-issuance pattern above at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526017691/ruby_3.0_prospectus_supp.htm and the F-3 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312525326983/rzlv-20251219.htm . The cash figures themselves rest on one body and on retail paraphrase, which is the weakest link in this finding.
